title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
abstract: arXiv:2610.13910v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly analyze and reason about images, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations faithfully encode the structured relations required for such reasoning. We introduce EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), a metric for testing whether representations consistently encode concepts under controlled one-concept interventions, and CASP-VL (Causally controlled Spatial Perturbations for Vision-Language models), a benchmark of causally controlled spatial perturbations derived from Visual Genome scene graphs. Across multiple VLM architectures, we find that spatial relations are represented substantially less faithfully than lexical information, even when the same models score well above chance on compositional benchmarks. translated_title: 当视觉语言模型破坏其所知：空间表征低于词汇先验
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）越来越多地被用于分析和推理图像，但尚不清楚其内部表征是否忠实地编码了此类推理所需的结构化关系。我们提出了EICS（评估不变概念稳定性），一种用于测试表征在受控单概念干预下是否一致编码概念的度量指标；同时提出CASP-VL（面向视觉语言模型的因果控制空间扰动），一个基于Visual Genome场景图构建的因果控制空间扰动基准。在多个VLM架构上，我们发现空间关系的表征远不如词汇信息忠实，即使这些模型在组合性基准测试中的得分远高于随机水平。进一步分析表明，空间关系在谓词自身的词元处是可识别的，但当句子被聚合为全局表征时便会丢失……
tldr: 研究发现视觉语言模型对空间关系的内部表征远不如词汇信息忠实——空间关系虽可在谓词词元层面识别，但在聚合为全局句子表征时会丢失，导致空间表征低于词汇先验，即使模型在组合性基准上表现良好。
